sanskrit: tvaṃ hi śakto raṇe jetuṃ sakarṇān api kauravān nānyo yudhi yudhāṃ śreṣṭha satyam etad bravīmi te
english: For you alone are able in battle to conquer the Kauravas, Karṇa and all; no other warrior can, O best of fighters. This truth I tell you.

sanskrit: etat kṛtvā mahat karma hatvā karṇaṃ mahāratham kṛtārthaḥ saphalaḥ pārtha sukhī bhava narottama
english: Having accomplished this great deed, having slain Karṇa the mighty chariot-warrior, your purpose fulfilled and your labor rewarded, O Pārtha, be happy, O best of men.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa keśavasya bībhatsuḥ śrutvā bhārata bhāṣitam viśokaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭaś ca kṣaṇena samapadyata
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard the words of Keśava, O Bhārata, Bībhatsu in a moment became free of sorrow and filled with delight.

sanskrit: tato jyām anumṛjyāśu vyākṣipad gāṇḍivaṃ dhanuḥ dadhre karṇavināśāya keśavaṃ cābhyabhāṣata
english: Then, stroking the bowstring, he swiftly drew the Gāṇḍīva bow, resolved upon Karṇa's destruction, and spoke to Keśava.

sanskrit: tvayā nāthena govinda dhruva eṣa jayo mama prasanno yasya me 'dya tvaṃ bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ
english: With you as my protector, Govinda, this victory of mine is assured—you who are gracious to me this day, lord of what has been, what shall be, and what is.

sanskrit: tvatsahāyo hy ahaṃ kṛṣṇa trīṃl lokān vai samāgatān prāpayeyaṃ paraṃ lokaṃ kim u karṇaṃ mahāraṇe
english: With you as my ally, Kṛṣṇa, even the three worlds gathered together I could dispatch to the world beyond—how much more then Karṇa in this great battle?

sanskrit: paśyāmi dravatīṃ senāṃ pāñcālānāṃ janārdana paśyāmi karṇaṃ samare vicarantam abhītavat
english: I see the army of the Pāñcālas fleeing, Janārdana; I see Karṇa ranging fearlessly through the fight.

sanskrit: bhārgavāstraṃ ca paśyāmi vicarantaṃ samantataḥ sṛṣṭaṃ karṇena vārṣṇeya śakreṇeva mahāśanim
english: And I see the Bhārgava weapon ranging on every side, loosed by Karṇa, O Vārṣṇeya, as Śakra looses the mighty thunderbolt.

sanskrit: ayaṃ khalu sa saṃgrāmo yatra kṛṣṇa mayā kṛtam kathayiṣyanti bhūtāni yāvad bhūmir dhariṣyati
english: This indeed is that battle, Kṛṣṇa, in which my deeds living beings will recount for as long as the earth shall endure.

sanskrit: adya kṛṣṇa vikarṇā me karṇaṃ neṣyanti mṛtyave gāṇḍīvamuktāḥ kṣiṇvanto mama hastapracoditāḥ
english: This day, Kṛṣṇa, my barbless shafts, loosed from the Gāṇḍīva and driven by my hand, shall bring Karṇa to his death, wearing him down.

sanskrit: adya rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ svāṃ buddhim avamaṃsyate duryodhanam arājyārhaṃ yayā rājye 'bhyaṣecayat
english: This day King Dhṛtarāṣṭra shall despise his own judgment, by which he consecrated Duryodhana—unfit for kingship—to the throne.

sanskrit: adya rājyāt sukhāc caiva śriyo rāṣṭrāt tathā purāt putrebhyaś ca mahābāho dhṛtarāṣṭro viyokṣyate
english: This day, O mighty-armed one, Dhṛtarāṣṭra shall be parted from his kingdom and his ease, from fortune, realm, and city, and from his sons.

sanskrit: adya duryodhano rājā jīvitāc ca nirāśakaḥ bhaviṣyati hate karṇe kṛṣṇa satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: This day, when Karṇa is slain, King Duryodhana shall despair even of his life, Kṛṣṇa—this truth I tell you.

sanskrit: adya dṛṣṭvā mayā karṇaṃ śarair viśakalīkṛtam smaratāṃ tava vākyāni śamaṃ prati janeśvaraḥ
english: This day, beholding Karṇa torn to shreds by my arrows, the lord of men shall remember your words spoken in favor of peace.

sanskrit: adyāsau saubalaḥ kṛṣṇa glahaṃ jānātu vai śarān durodaraṃ ca gāṇḍīvaṃ maṇḍalaṃ ca rathaṃ mama
english: This day, Kṛṣṇa, let that son of Subala learn that my arrows are the dice, the Gāṇḍīva the gaming-board, and my chariot the gaming-circle.

sanskrit: yo 'sau raṇe naraṃ nānyaṃ pṛthivyām abhimanyate tasyādya sūtaputrasya bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam gāṇḍīvasṛṣṭā dāsyanti karṇasya paramāṃ gatim
english: That son of the charioteer who in battle deems no other man on earth his equal—this day the earth shall drink his blood, and the shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva shall send Karṇa to his final end.

sanskrit: adya tapsyati rādheyaḥ pāñcālīṃ yat tadābravīt sabhāmadhye vacaḥ krūraṃ kutsayan pāṇḍavān prati
english: This day Rādheya shall repent the cruel words he spoke against the daughter of Pāñcāla in the midst of the assembly, reviling the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: ye vai ṣaṇḍhatilās tatra bhavitāro 'dya te tilāḥ hate vaikartane karṇe sūtaputre durātmani
english: Those who were there called barren sesame seeds shall this day become true seeds, once Karṇa Vaikartana, the vile son of the charioteer, is slain.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vaḥ pāṇḍuputrebhyas trāsyāmīti yad abravīt anṛtaṃ tat kariṣyanti māmakā niśitāḥ śarāḥ
english: When he declared, 'I shall save you from the sons of Pāṇḍu,' my sharpened arrows shall prove that boast a lie.

sanskrit: hantāhaṃ pāṇḍavān sarvān saputrān iti yo 'bravīt tam adya karṇaṃ hantāsmi miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: He who said, 'I shall slay all the Pāṇḍavas together with their sons'—that very Karṇa I shall this day slay before the eyes of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: yasya vīrye samāśvasya dhārtarāṣṭro bṛhanmanāḥ avāmanyata durbuddhir nityam asmān durātmavān tam adya karṇaṃ rādheyaṃ hantāsmi madhusūdana
english: He in whose valor the arrogant son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra trusted, that foolish and evil-souled one who ever held us in contempt—that Karṇa Rādheya I shall this day slay, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: adya karṇe hate kṛṣṇa dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ sarājakāḥ vidravantu diśo bhītāḥ siṃhatrastā mṛgā iva
english: This day, when Karṇa is slain, Kṛṣṇa, let the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra with their kings flee in terror to every quarter, like deer scattered by a lion.

sanskrit: adya duryodhano rājā pṛthivīm anvavekṣatām hate karṇe mayā saṃkhye saputre sasuhṛjjane
english: This day let King Duryodhana gaze upon the earth, when Karṇa is slain by me in the fray together with his sons and his kinsmen and friends.

sanskrit: adya karṇaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭro 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ jānātu māṃ raṇe kṛṣṇa pravaraṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: This day, beholding Karṇa slain, let the wrathful son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra know me, Kṛṣṇa, to be the foremost of all bowmen in battle.

sanskrit: adyāham anṛṇaḥ kṛṣṇa bhaviṣyāmi dhanurbhṛtām krodhasya ca kurūṇāṃ ca śarāṇāṃ gāṇḍivasya ca
english: This day, Kṛṣṇa, I shall become free of my debt to the bearers of bows, to my own wrath, to the Kurus, to my arrows, and to the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: adya duḥkham ahaṃ mokṣye trayodaśasamārjitam hatvā karṇaṃ raṇe kṛṣṇa śambaraṃ maghavān iva
english: This day I shall be freed of the grief amassed through thirteen years, by slaying Karṇa in battle, Kṛṣṇa, as Maghavat slew Śambara.

sanskrit: adya karṇe hate yuddhe somakānāṃ mahārathāḥ kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ ca manyantāṃ mitrakāryepsavo yudhi
english: This day, when Karṇa is slain in battle, let the great chariot-warriors of the Somakas, eager to serve their friends in the fight, deem their task accomplished.

sanskrit: na jāne ca kathaṃ prītiḥ śaineyasyādya mādhava bhaviṣyati hate karṇe mayi cāpi jayādhike
english: And I do not know, Mādhava, how great this day shall be the joy of the grandson of Śini, when Karṇa is slain and I emerge crowned with victory.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hatvā raṇe karṇaṃ putraṃ cāsya mahāratham prītiṃ dāsyāmi bhīmasya yamayoḥ sātyaker api
english: By slaying Karṇa and his son, the mighty chariot-warrior, in battle, I shall give delight to Bhīma, to the twins, and to Sātyaki as well.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍibhyāṃ pāñcālānāṃ ca mādhava adhyānṛṇyaṃ gamiṣyāmi hatvā karṇaṃ mahāraṇe
english: To Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin and to the Pāñcālas, Mādhava, I shall discharge my debt by slaying Karṇa in this great battle.

sanskrit: adya paśyantu saṃgrāme dhanaṃjayam amarṣaṇam yudhyantaṃ kauravān saṃkhye pātayantaṃ ca sūtajam bhavatsakāśe vakṣye ca punar evātmasaṃstavam
english: This day let them behold in the fight Dhanaṃjaya, unyielding in his wrath, battling the Kauravas in the fray and bringing down the charioteer's son. And in your presence I shall once more speak my own praise.

sanskrit: dhanurvede matsamo nāsti loke; parākrame vā mama ko 'sti tulyaḥ ko vāpy anyo matsamo 'sti kṣamāyāṃ; tathā krodhe sadṛśo 'nyo na me 'sti
english: In the science of archery there is none in the world my equal, nor in valor who is a match for me. Who else is my peer in forbearance? And in wrath too there is no other like me.

sanskrit: ahaṃ dhanuṣmān asurān surāṃś ca; sarvāṇi bhūtāni ca saṃgatāni svabāhuvīryād gamaye parābhavaṃ; matpauruṣaṃ viddhi paraḥ parebhyaḥ
english: With bow in hand, asuras and gods and all creatures gathered together, by the might of my own arms I would drive to ruin. Know my prowess to be supreme above the supreme.

sanskrit: śarārciṣā gāṇḍivenāham ekaḥ; sarvān kurūn bāhlikāṃś cābhipatya himātyaye kakṣagato yathāgnis; tahā daheyaṃ sagaṇān prasahya
english: With the Gāṇḍīva flaming with arrows, I alone, falling upon all the Kurus and the Bāhlīkas, would burn them and their hosts by force, as fire reaching dry brushwood at winter's end.

sanskrit: pāṇau pṛṣatkā likhitā mamaite; dhanuś ca savye nihitaṃ sabāṇam pādau ca me sarathau sadhvajau ca; na mādṛśaṃ yuddhagataṃ jayanti
english: These shafts are as if drawn upon my hand; the bow with its arrow rests fixed in my left hand; my feet stand firm with chariot and banner. None can conquer one like me once I have entered the battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca teṣām anīkāni bṛhaddhvajāni; raṇe samṛddhāni samāgatāni garjanti bherīninadonmukhāni; meghair yathā meghagaṇās tapānte
english: Saṃjaya said: Their battalions, with towering banners, mighty and arrayed for war, came together roaring with the thunder of kettle-drums, as cloud-masses thunder against cloud at the close of the hot season.

sanskrit: mahāgajābhrākulam astratoyaṃ; vāditranemītalaśabdavac ca hiraṇyacitrāyudhavaidyutaṃ ca; mahārathair āvṛtaśabdavac ca
english: Thick with great elephants like storm-clouds, its rain the weapons, resounding with the noise of instruments, chariot-rims, and palms; lightning-bright with weapons adorned in gold, and clamorous with the press of mighty chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: tad bhīmavegaṃ rudhiraughavāhi; khaḍgākulaṃ kṣatriyajīvavāhi anārtavaṃ krūram aniṣṭavarṣaṃ; babhūva tat saṃharaṇaṃ prajānām
english: Of terrible swiftness, bearing torrents of blood, thronged with swords, carrying off the lives of warriors—untimely, cruel, raining down what none desired—it became the destruction of living beings.

sanskrit: rathān sasūtān sahayān gajāṃś ca; sarvān arīn mṛtyuvaśaṃ śaraughaiḥ ninye hayāṃś caiva tathā sasādīn; padātisaṃghāṃś ca tathaiva pārthaḥ
english: Chariots with their drivers and horses, elephants, and all his foes, Pārtha brought under the sway of death with floods of arrows—horses with their riders, and the throngs of foot-soldiers likewise.

sanskrit: kṛpaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca raṇe sametau; duryodhanaṃ sātyakir abhyagacchata śrutaśravā droṇasutena sārdhaṃ; yudhāmanyuś citrasenena cāpi
english: Kṛpa and Śikhaṇḍin met together in battle; Sātyaki advanced upon Duryodhana; Śrutaśravā closed with the son of Droṇa, and Yudhāmanyu with Citrasena.

sanskrit: karṇasya putras tu rathī suṣeṇaṃ; samāgataḥ sṛñjayāṃś cottamaujāḥ gāndhārarājaṃ sahadevaḥ kṣudhārto; maharṣabhaṃ siṃha ivābhyadhāvat
english: The son of Karṇa, the chariot-warrior, came against Suṣeṇa; Uttamaujas against the Sṛñjayas; and Sahadeva, ravenous, rushed upon the king of Gāndhāra as a lion upon a great bull.

sanskrit: śatānīko nākuliḥ karṇaputraṃ; yuvā yuvānaṃ vṛṣasenaṃ śaraughaiḥ samārdayat karṇasutaś ca vīraḥ; pāñcāleyaṃ śaravarṣair anekaiḥ
english: Śatānīka, son of Nakula, a youth, assailed the youthful Vṛṣasena, son of Karṇa, with floods of arrows; and the heroic son of Karṇa, in turn, struck the prince of Pāñcāla with many showers of shafts.

sanskrit: ratharṣabhaḥ kṛtavarmāṇam ārcchan; mādrīputro nakulaś citrayodhī pāñcālānām adhipo yājñaseniḥ; senāpatiṃ karṇam ārcchat sasainyam
english: The bull among chariot-warriors, Nakula son of Mādrī, skilled in varied modes of fighting, came against Kṛtavarman; and the lord of the Pāñcālas, son of Yajñasena, came against the commander Karṇa with his troops.

sanskrit: duḥśāsano bhārata bhāratī ca; saṃśaptakānāṃ pṛtanā samṛddhā bhīmaṃ raṇe śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaṃ; tadā samārcchat tam asahyavegam
english: Duḥśāsana, O Bhārata, and the mighty host of the Saṃśaptakas of the Bhāratas then closed in battle with Bhīma, foremost of weapon-bearers, whose onset none could withstand.

sanskrit: karṇātmajaṃ tatra jaghāna śūras; tathācchinac cottamaujāḥ prasahya tasyottamāṅgaṃ nipapāta bhūmau; ninādayad gāṃ ninadena khaṃ ca
english: There the hero Uttamaujas struck down the son of Karṇa and forcibly severed his head, which fell to the ground, making the earth and the sky resound with its noise.

sanskrit: suṣeṇaśīrṣaṃ patitaṃ pṛthivyāṃ; vilokya karṇo 'tha tadārtarūpaḥ krodhād dhayāṃs tasya rathaṃ dhvajaṃ ca; bāṇaiḥ sudhārair niśitair nyakṛntat
english: Beholding Suṣeṇa's head fallen to the earth, Karṇa, then stricken with grief, in his wrath cut down with keen, well-honed arrows the horses, the chariot, and the banner of his foe.

sanskrit: sa tūttamaujā niśitaiḥ pṛṣatkair; vivyādha khaḍgena ca bhāsvareṇa pārṣṇiṃ hayāṃś caiva kṛpasya hatvā; śikhaṇḍivāhaṃ sa tato 'bhyarohat
english: But Uttamaujas pierced him with sharp shafts, and with a gleaming sword slew the flank-guards and the horses of Kṛpa, and then mounted the chariot of Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: kṛpaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā virathaṃ rathastho; naicchac charais tāḍayituṃ śikhaṇḍī taṃ drauṇir āvārya rathaṃ kṛpaṃ sma; samujjahre paṅkagatāṃ yathā gām
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, mounted on his chariot, seeing Kṛpa deprived of his car, would not strike him with arrows; and the son of Droṇa, covering him, lifted Kṛpa onto his chariot as one would raise a cow sunk in the mire.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavarmā niśitaiḥ pṛṣatkais; tavātmajānām anilātmajo vai atāpayat sainyam atīva bhīmaḥ; kāle śucau madhyagato yathārkaḥ
english: Golden-armored Bhīma, son of the Wind, with sharp shafts scorched the army of your sons most terribly, as the sun set in mid-sky scorches in the bright hot season.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca atha tv idānīṃ tumule vimarde; dviṣadbhir eko bahubhiḥ samāvṛtaḥ mahābhaye sārathim ity uvāca; bhīmaś camūṃ vārayan dhārtarāṣṭrīm tvaṃ sārathe yāhi javena vāhair; nayāmy etān dhārtarāṣṭrān yamāya
english: Saṃjaya said: Now, in the tumultuous fray, surrounded—one against many foes—in that great peril, Bhīma, holding back the army of the Dhārtarāṣṭras, spoke thus to his charioteer: 'Drive on, charioteer, swiftly with the horses; I shall send these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra to Yama.'

sanskrit: saṃcodito bhīmasenena caivaṃ; sa sārathiḥ putrabalaṃ tvadīyam prāyāt tataḥ sārathir ugravego; yato bhīmas tad balaṃ gantum aicchat
english: Thus urged by Bhīmasena, the charioteer of fierce speed drove on toward the host of your sons, to wherever Bhīma wished that army to be reached.

sanskrit: tato 'pare nāgarathāśvapattibhiḥ; pratyudyayuḥ kuravas taṃ samantāt bhīmasya vāhāgryam udāravegaṃ; samantato bāṇagaṇair nijaghnuḥ
english: Then others among the Kurus advanced against him on every side with elephants, chariots, horse, and foot, and on all sides struck Bhīma's swift, high-mettled horses with clouds of arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarān āpatato mahātmā; ciccheda bāṇais tapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ te vai nipetus tapanīyapuṅkhā; dvidhā tridhā bhīmaśarair nikṛttāḥ
english: Then the great-souled one cut down the oncoming arrows with shafts feathered in gold; and those gold-feathered shafts fell, cleft in two and in three by Bhīma's arrows.

sanskrit: tato rājan nāgarathāśvayūnāṃ; bhīmāhatānāṃ tava rājamadhye ghoro ninādaḥ prababhau narendra; vajrāhatānām iva parvatānām
english: Then, O king, amid your hosts, from the elephants, chariots, and horses struck down by Bhīma there arose a fearful roar, O lord of men, like that of mountains riven by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāś ca narendramukhyā; nirbhinnā vai bhīmasenapravekaiḥ bhīmaṃ samantāt samare 'dhyarohan; vṛkṣaṃ śakuntā iva puṣpahetoḥ
english: And those foremost of kings, slaughtered and pierced through by Bhīmasena's choicest shafts, swarmed upon Bhīma in the battle from every side, as birds settle upon a tree for the sake of its blossoms.

sanskrit: tato 'bhipātaṃ tava sainyamadhye; prāduścakre vegam ivāttavegaḥ yathāntakāle kṣapayan didhakṣur; bhūtāntakṛtkāla ivāttadaṇḍaḥ
english: Then, swift as one possessed of utmost speed, he made his onslaught in the midst of your army, eager to consume and destroy, like Time itself with rod in hand bringing creatures to their end at the hour of doom.

sanskrit: tasyātivegasya raṇe 'tivegaṃ; nāśaknuvan dhārayituṃ tvadīyāḥ vyāttānanasyāpatato yathaiva; kālasya kāle harataḥ prajā vai
english: His exceeding onrush in battle your men could not withstand, even as none can withstand the gaping, swift-falling onset of Time bearing off creatures at the appointed hour.

sanskrit: tato balaṃ bhārata bhāratānāṃ; pradahyamānaṃ samare mahātman bhītaṃ diśo 'kīryata bhīmanunnaṃ; mahānilenābhragaṇo yathaiva
english: Then the host of the Bhāratas, O great-souled Bhārata, burning in the battle and stricken with fear, scattered to every quarter, driven by Bhīma, as a mass of clouds is scattered by a mighty wind.

sanskrit: tato dhīmān sārathim abravīd balī; sa bhīmasenaḥ punar eva hṛṣṭaḥ sūtābhijānīhi parān svakān vā; rathān dhvajāṃś cāpatataḥ sametān yudhyann ahaṃ nābhijānāmi kiṃ cin; mā sainyaṃ svaṃ chādayiṣye pṛṣatkaiḥ
english: Then the wise and mighty Bhīmasena, joyful once more, spoke to his charioteer: 'Charioteer, mark whether these chariots and banners closing upon us are foes or our own; for fighting on I can discern nothing—let me not cover my own troops with my shafts.'

sanskrit: arīn viśokābhinirīkṣya sarvato; manas tu cintā pradunoti me bhṛśam rājāturo nāgamad yat kirīṭī; bahūni duḥkhāny abhijāto 'smi sūta
english: 'Viśoka, look out upon the foes on every side; yet anxiety sorely afflicts my mind. The king is in distress, and the Diademed One has not come; many griefs, O charioteer, are mine.'

sanskrit: etad duḥkhaṃ sārathe dharmarājo; yan māṃ hitvā yātavāñ śatrumadhye nainaṃ jīvan nāpi jānāmy ajīvan; bībhatsuṃ vā tan mamādyātiduḥkham
english: 'This is my grief, charioteer—that the Dharma-king, leaving me, has gone into the midst of the foe. I know not whether he lives or lives no longer, nor whether Bībhatsu lives; that is my deepest sorrow this day.'

sanskrit: so 'haṃ dviṣatsainyam udagrakalpaṃ; vināśayiṣye paramapratītaḥ etān nihatyājimadhye sametān; prīto bhaviṣyāmi saha tvayādya
english: 'I therefore shall destroy this towering host of the enemy, supremely confident; and having slain these gathered together in the midst of battle, I shall this day be glad together with you.'

sanskrit: sarvāṃs tūṇīrān mārgaṇān vānvavekṣya; kiṃ śiṣṭaṃ syāt sāyakānāṃ rathe me kā vā jātiḥ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ ca teṣāṃ; jñātvā vyaktaṃ tan mamācakṣva sūta
english: 'Look over all the quivers and the shafts: what store of arrows remains in my chariot, of what kinds, and how many? Knowing this clearly, tell it to me, charioteer.'

sanskrit: viśoka uvāca ṣaṇmārgaṇānām ayutāni vīra; kṣurāś ca bhallāś ca tathāyutākhyāḥ nārācānāṃ dve sahasre tu vīra; trīṇy eva ca pradarāṇāṃ ca pārtha
english: Viśoka said: Sixty thousand arrows there are, O hero; razor-shafts and broad-headed shafts numbering ten thousand each; two thousand iron arrows, O hero, and three thousand barbed darts, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: asty āyudhaṃ pāṇḍaveyāvaśiṣṭaṃ; na yad vahec chakaṭaṃ ṣaḍgavīyam etad vidvan muñca sahasraśo 'pi; gadāsibāhudraviṇaṃ ca te 'sti
english: There remains weaponry yet, O scion of Pāṇḍu, such as a cart drawn by six oxen could not bear. Knowing this, loose them by the thousands; and you have besides your mace, your sword, and the wealth of your own arms.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca sūtādyemaṃ paśya bhīmapramuktaiḥ; saṃbhindadbhiḥ pārthivān āśuvegaiḥ ugrair bāṇair āhavaṃ ghorarūpaṃ; naṣṭādityaṃ mṛtyulokena tulyam
english: Bhīma said: Charioteer, behold this day a battle of terrible aspect, where kings are pierced through by swift, fierce arrows loosed by Bhīma—the sun blotted out, a scene like the world of death itself.

sanskrit: adyaiva tad viditaṃ pārthivānāṃ; bhaviṣyati ākumāraṃ ca sūta nimagno vā samare bhīmasena; ekaḥ kurūn vā samare vijetā
english: This very day, charioteer, it shall be known to all the kings, down to the very children, whether Bhīmasena has sunk down in the battle, or whether alone he is the conqueror of the Kurus in the fray.

sanskrit: sarve saṃkhye kuravo niṣpatantu; māṃ vā lokāḥ kīrtayantv ākumāram sarvān ekas tān ahaṃ pātayiṣye; te vā sarve bhīmasenaṃ tudantu
english: Let all the Kurus fall upon me in battle, or let the worlds, down to the children, sing my praise: alone I shall bring them all down, or let them all together strike at Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: āśāstāraḥ karma cāpy uttamaṃ vā; tan me devāḥ kevalaṃ sādhayantu āyātv ihādyārjunaḥ śatrughātī; śakras tūrṇaṃ yajña ivopahūtaḥ
english: May the gods, my well-wishers, alone bring to fulfillment this highest deed of mine. Let Arjuna, slayer of foes, come hither this day, swiftly as Śakra summoned to a sacrifice.

sanskrit: īkṣasvaitāṃ bhāratīṃ dīryamāṇām; ete kasmād vidravante narendrāḥ vyaktaṃ dhīmān savyasācī narāgryaḥ; sainyaṃ hy etac chādayaty āśu bāṇaiḥ
english: Behold this Bhārata host breaking apart: why do these kings flee? Surely the wise Savyasācin, foremost of men, is swiftly covering this army with his arrows.

sanskrit: paśya dhvajāṃś ca dravato viśoka; nāgān hayān pattisaṃghāṃś ca saṃkhye rathān viśīrṇāñ śaraśaktitāḍitān; paśyasvaitān rathinaś caiva sūta
english: Look upon the banners fleeing, Viśoka—the elephants, the horses, and the throngs of foot-soldiers in the fray; behold the chariots shattered, struck down by arrow and lance, and behold these chariot-warriors too, charioteer.

sanskrit: āpūryate kauravī cāpy abhīkṣṇaṃ; senā hy asau subhṛśaṃ hanyamānā dhanaṃjayasyāśanitulyavegair; grastā śarair barhisuvarṇavājaiḥ
english: That Kaurava army, ever filling its ranks anew yet most grievously slaughtered, is devoured by the arrows of Dhanaṃjaya—swift as the thunderbolt, fledged with peacock-feathers and gold.

sanskrit: ete dravanti sma rathāśvanāgāḥ; padātisaṃghān avamardayantaḥ saṃmuhyamānāḥ kauravāḥ sarva eva; dravanti nāgā iva dāvabhītāḥ hāhākṛtāś caiva raṇe viśoka; muñcanti nādān vipulān gajendrāḥ
english: These chariots, horses, and elephants flee, trampling down the bands of foot-soldiers; bewildered, all the Kauravas flee like elephants in terror of a forest fire; and crying woe in the battle, Viśoka, the lordly elephants send forth vast bellowings.

sanskrit: viśoka uvāca sarve kāmāḥ pāṇḍava te samṛddhāḥ; kapidhvajo dṛśyate hastisainye nīlād dhanād vidyutam uccarantīṃ; tathāpaśyaṃ visphurad vai dhanus tat
english: Viśoka said: All your desires, O Pāṇḍava, are fulfilled: the ape-bannered one is seen amid the elephant-host. As lightning leaping forth from a dark cloud, so I behold that bow flashing.

sanskrit: kapir hy asau vīkṣyate sarvato vai; dhvajāgram āruhya dhanaṃjayasya divākarābho maṇir eṣa divyo; vibhrājate caiva kirīṭasaṃsthaḥ
english: That ape is seen on every side, mounted upon the banner-tip of Dhanaṃjaya; and this divine jewel, bright as the sun, blazes set within his diadem.

sanskrit: pārśve bhīmaṃ pāṇḍurābhraprakāśaṃ; paśyemaṃ tvaṃ devadattaṃ sughoṣam abhīśuhastasya janārdanasya; vigāhamānasya camūṃ pareṣām
english: At his side, terrible and shining like a white cloud, behold the conch Devadatta of fair sound, in the hand of Janārdana who, reins in hand, plunges into the army of the foe.

sanskrit: raviprabhaṃ vajranābhaṃ kṣurāntaṃ; pārśve sthitaṃ paśya janārdanasya cakraṃ yaśo vardhayat keśavasya; sadārcitaṃ yadubhiḥ paśya vīra
english: Bright as the sun, with adamant nave and razor-edged rim, behold the discus standing at the side of Janārdana, ever increasing the glory of Keśava and forever revered by the Yadus—behold it, hero.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca dadāmi te grāmavarāṃś caturdaśa; priyākhyāne sārathe suprasannaḥ dasīśataṃ cāpi rathāṃś ca viṃśatiṃ; yad arjunaṃ vedayase viśoka
english: Bhīma said: For this welcome tidings, charioteer, well pleased I give you fourteen choice villages, a hundred handmaids, and twenty chariots besides—since you announce Arjuna to me, Viśoka.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śrutvā ca rathanirghoṣaṃ siṃhanādaṃ ca saṃyuge arjunaḥ prāha govindaṃ śīghraṃ codaya vājinaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing the rumble of the chariot and the lion-roar in the battle, Arjuna said to Govinda: 'Drive the horses swiftly.'

sanskrit: arjunasya vacaḥ śrutvā govindo 'rjunam abravīt eṣa gacchāmi sukṣipraṃ yatra bhīmo vyavasthitaḥ
english: Hearing Arjuna's words, Govinda said to Arjuna: 'I go this instant, with all speed, to where Bhīma stands his ground.'
